answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The bridge multiplier is published, charged in saffron, and kernel lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1414 identities would post 2501 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
